results.claim: Yettinahole (CAG 2025 PA, Ch II): approved July 2012 Rs 8,323.50 cr; revised Rs 23,251.66 cr Jan 2023; Rs 15,297.03 cr spent by March 2024; no water delivered; no DPR fixed a completion date; state released only 25-54% of yearly requested budget 2018-23.
results.correct_text: CAG (Report No. 10, Implementation of Yettinahole Integrated Drinking Water Project, tabled 29 Jan 2026) found the project, approved in July 2012 at Rs 8,323.50 crore, was revised to Rs 12,912.36 crore (Feb 2014) and Rs 23,251.66 crore (Jan 2023); Rs 15,297.03 crore (GoK grants Rs 12,535.59 cr plus VJNL borrowings Rs 2,567.66 cr) was spent up to 2023-24 (March 2024); none of the DPRs specified a completion period; the project 'could not be made operational even after 12 years of conception' and was still in progress in December 2024; and the Government provided only 25 to 54 per cent of VJNL's budget requirements in 2018-19 to 2022-23.
results.page_or_para: Ch II summary (report p.7, PDF p.3); para 2.1 Table 2.1 (report p.9); para 2.1.1 (PDF p.7); para 2.2 Table 2.5 and 2.2.1 (report p.18, PDF p.14). Report identity: https://cag.gov.in/en/audit-report/details/123863
results.note: All numbers match. Corrections: (1) 'no water delivered' is stronger than CAG, which says the project 'could not be made operational' / intended objective not achieved; use that wording. (2) The 25-54% covers grants PLUS VJNL borrowings (Table 2.5 'Budget Allocation/Releases' includes borrowings), so write 'Government provided', not 'state released'. Table 2.5 also gives short release of 46-75% for 2018-19 to 2023-24. (3) Report is No. 10 'for the year ended March 2023', tabled 29 Jan 2026. Side note: CAG prints the increase as Rs 14,928.19 cr but 23,251.66 - 8,323.50 = 14,928.16; drafts use both values - say 'about Rs 14,928 crore'.

results.claim: Smart Cities (CAG Report No. 11 of 2025): received vs spent to June 2024 Bengaluru 812/988, Tumakuru 855/990, Hubballi-Dharwad 791.22/990 (6 of 62 awarded on time), Belagavi 859.14/990 (3 of 107 on time); Mangaluru Rs 51.85 cr facing lapse, Rs 9.44 cr sewer 'unfruitful', 19 of 35 basic-amenity projects complete; Tumakuru Rs 20.71 cr trauma centre idle two years; Shivamogga no full-time CEO 5 years; Davanagere command centre 3 yr 4 months late.
results.correct_text: CAG Report No. 11 of 2025 (Smart City Mission, tabled 29 Jan 2026) shows, as of June 2024: Bengaluru spent Rs 812.06 cr of Rs 988 cr received; Tumakuru Rs 855.15 cr of Rs 990 cr; Hubballi-Dharwad Rs 791.22 cr of Rs 990 cr, with 6 of 62 projects awarded within the stipulated timeline; Belagavi Rs 859.14 cr of Rs 990 cr, with 3 of 107 awarded on time. In Mangaluru, dropped works left Rs 51.85 cr of allocated funds that MSCL 'will not be able to utilise', Rs 9.44 cr spent on underground-drainage packages was rendered 'unfruitful', and 19 of 35 basic-amenity projects were complete. Tumakuru's Rs 20.71 cr transferred to the Health department for a district-hospital trauma care centre (16 Aug 2019) was utilised only in December 2021, 'after a gap of two years'. Shivamogga's SPV had no full-time CEO from 7 Feb 2017 to 3 Mar 2022 (5 years). Davanagere's command centre went live on 27 Feb 2023 against a scheduled 10 Oct 2019, a delay of 3 years 4 months.
results.page_or_para: Ch 3 Table 3.1 (report p.16) and Table 3.3 (report p.21); Ch 4 Table 4.2 (CEO), Table 4.3 (report p.27, awards), Table 4.5 (ICCC), para 4.10 (report p.52, Rs 51.85 cr), Table 4.12 and para 4.11.1 (report p.53). Report identity: https://cag.gov.in/en/audit-report/details/123892
results.note: All figures match. Wording caveats: (a) Mangaluru Rs 51.85 cr appears in PDF text as '51.8541' (footnote 41: Rs 9.92 cr jetty + Rs 41.93 cr Nayar Kudru); State's April 2025 reply says Rs 30 cr was reallocated to a road bridge and the rest to a DC-office project, so 'facing lapse' should carry that reply. (b) Tumakuru money sat with the Health department, not the SPV. (c) Report number and tabling date confirmed on the CAG details page.

results.claim: KKRDB (CAG Report No. 10 of 2022): 74% of released funds spent with 70% physical progress; Rs 387.52 cr loss of assistance (5,244.34 of 5,631.86, 2016-17 to 2020-21); 3,731 works worth Rs 738.65 cr cancelled 2013-21; idle works Kalaburagi theme park Rs 5.60 cr, Yadgir textile centre Rs 5.02 cr, Raichur road Rs 1.29 cr; PCI growth state 74.84% vs Kalaburagi 47.96%; child anaemia NFHS-4 to 5 for Yadgir, Kalaburagi, Raichur.
results.correct_text: CAG Report No. 10 of 2022 (Functioning of KKRDB, tabled 23 Feb 2023) found the Board spent 74% of funds released over the last five years with physical progress of up to 70%; against Rs 5,631.86 cr allocated in 2016-17 to 2020-21 only Rs 5,244.34 cr was released, a 'loss of assistance' of Rs 387.52 cr because the Board had not used 75% of available funds (the Government disputes this); 3,731 works (13% of 28,038) estimated at Rs 738.65 cr were cancelled during 2013-21; Rs 5.60 cr spent on five abandoned works at Rajiv Gandhi Theme Park and Kotnoor D Park, Kalaburagi, was 'rendered wasteful'; a Rs 5.02 cr hi-tech textile training centre in Yadgir taluk, completed in 2018-19, stood idle; and a Manvi (Raichur) road stopped in June 2019 after Rs 1.29 cr. Per-capita income grew 74.84% statewide but 47.96% in Kalaburagi between 2013-14 and 2019-20. Anaemia in children aged 6-59 months rose from 74% to 76% in Yadgir, 72.4% to 75.1% in Kalaburagi and 70.6% to 73.6% in Raichur between NFHS-4 (2015-16) and NFHS-5, the three highest in the State.
results.page_or_para: Exec summary p.vii; Ch 5 Table 5.1 and para 5.2.2; Ch 4 works-status table (PDF p.3), paras 4.2.7, 4.2.8, 4.2.13; Ch 2 Table 2.2 (PCI) and Table 2.12 (child anaemia). Report number: CAG archive calm.cag.gov.in; details page https://cag.gov.in/en/audit-report/details/117967 (tabled 23 Feb 2023)
results.note: Numbers all match. Corrections: (1) Rs 5.60 cr is not one 'theme park': four works at Rajiv Gandhi Theme Park (Rs 3.15 cr) plus a concert stage at Kotnoor D Park (Rs 2.45 cr); CAG calls them 'abandoned'/'wasteful', not idle. (2) Raichur road was 'stopped'/'unproductive', not idle. (3) Loss of assistance: Government replied (July 2022) that 2019-20 was COVID-hit and Rs 100 cr of 2020-21 went to another society, 'hence no shortfall' - carry the dispute. (4) CAG labels NFHS-5 as '19-20'; NFHS-5 spans 2019-21 - say 'NFHS-5, as tabulated by CAG'. (5) Allocation check: 1,000+1,000+1,000+1,500+1,131.86 = 5,631.86.

results.claim: District Mineral Foundation (CAG 2025): Ballari collected Rs 1,912.55 cr, used Rs 629.62 cr (39.51%) to March 2023; statewide 1,826.46 of 4,003.51 cr. Find the report number.
results.correct_text: CAG Report No. 7 of 2025 (PMKKKY including District Mineral Foundation Trusts, tabled 17 Dec 2025) found Karnataka collected Rs 4,003.51 crore in DMF contributions and spent Rs 1,826.46 crore as of March 2023; in Ballari, Rs 629.62 crore (39.51%) of Rs 1,912.55 crore collected was utilised during 2015-16 to 2022-23, the lowest of the five test-checked districts.
results.page_or_para: Ch III Table 3.1 (state totals) and Table 3.2 (district-wise). Report identity: https://cag.gov.in/en/audit-report/details/123410
results.note: Report number = No. 7 of 2025, tabled 17 Dec 2025. Draft says Ballari is 'the lowest rate CAG found' - true only among the 5 selected districts (Ballari, Vijayanagara, Chitradurga, Bengaluru Urban, Gadag); say so.

results.claim: Mysuru 24x7 water (CAG Report No. 2 of 2017): Rs 271.56 cr spent without achieving 24x7; zones cut 69 to 47; NRW 25.7-37% vs 15%; Kabini augmentation Rs 95.71 cr, reservoirs not in use 2016.
results.correct_text: CAG Report No. 2 of 2017 found that despite an expenditure of Rs 271.56 crore (project cost Rs 229.94 cr plus Rs 41.62 cr for O&M), Mysuru did not get 24x7 water: coverage was cut from 69 to 47 Direct Metering Areas, and non-revenue water ranged from 25.69% to 37.01% against a 15% condition of approval. On the Kabini source-augmentation scheme (Rs 95.71 cr spent), none of the three master balancing reservoirs was in use at a joint inspection in February 2016.
results.page_or_para: PA 2.1 executive summary; para 2.1.11 project table and 2.1.11.1 (report p.37, PDF p.25); para 2.1.11.2 and footnote 19 (report p.39, PDF p.27)
results.note: 'Zones' = Direct Metering Areas (DMAs); use CAG's term. Exact NRW range 25.69-37.01%. Rs 271.56 cr includes the O&M provision. Reservoir finding is as of the Feb 2016 inspection; Government (Jan 2017) cited incomplete pumping station and no demand. Report number from the official file title.

results.claim: Kodagu (CAG Report No. 8 of 2025): Rs 57.04 cr unspent with the DC at 31 March 2023, highest of nine districts; no permanent flood-protection works.
results.correct_text: CAG Report No. 8 of 2025 (Disaster Management in Karnataka, tabled 17 Dec 2025) found Rs 57.04 crore unspent in the Kodagu Deputy Commissioner's PD account at the end of March 2023, the largest DC-level balance among the nine test-checked districts (none of Kodagu's five taluks furnished balance data); the Kodagu DC told audit that structural flood measures were not taken up and affected people were compensated instead.
results.page_or_para: Ch III Table 3.3 (report p.35, PDF p.9); Ch V structural-measures paragraph before Recommendation 13 (PDF pp.15-16). Report identity: https://cag.gov.in/en/audit-report/details/123611
results.note: 'Highest of nine' must be qualified as the DC PD-account balance: Belagavi's DC (51.08) + taluk (22.18) balances total Rs 73.26 cr, above Kodagu's 57.04, and Kodagu's taluk balances are unknown (0 of 5 furnished). 'No permanent flood-protection works' is stronger than the source: CAG says statewide that permanent structural measures were 'not initiated', and specifically that the DCs of Dakshina Kannada, Davanagere and Kodagu 'replied that structural measures were not taken up'. Attribute it to the DC's reply.
